newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa shares its peace with Ireland foes.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa shares its peace with Ireland foes.

text.p: South Africa will share the lessons of its transition from conflict to democracy with Northern Ireland's foes at the weekend, but will address Sinn Fein and the Ulster Unionists separately, a minister said on Friday.

South African Minister of Constitutional Affairs Mohammed Valli Moosa said nine Northern Ireland political parties would gather at Arniston, east of Cape Town, but would not directly discuss the breakdown in their own peace efforts.
"This is not a continuation or part of negotiations on the Northern Ireland question. It is about discussing the South African transition," he told a news conference.
"It is not about mediation of any kind...It is also not about South Africa advising on the Northern Ireland question. We do not feel that we have the expertise or knowledge to do that."

The minister said arrangements were in place to ensure that the unionists did not have to meet or see the Sinn Fein delegation during the three-day conference in a former missile-testing complex that is now a nature reserve.
Valli Moosa was the deputy chief negotiator for Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC) in talks between 1990 and 1996 with the former white National Party government of F.W. de Klerk.
South Africa's bloody racial conflict largely ended after de Klerk repudiated apartheid in 1990, freed Mandela from prison and legalised his ANC.
The country held peaceful elections in 1994 and then spent two years negotiating a permanent post-apartheid constitution that went into force in February.

"They want to know what happened in South Africa. It is a very natural thing for people involved in conflict, especially where there is a possibility for negotiations, to look closely at what happened in South Africa.
"We think that if it can help the Irish political parties to come even ever so slightly closer to each other a useful purpose will have been served," Valli Moosa said.

He said the Ulster Unionist Party delegation headed by party leader David Trimble and the Democratic Unionist Party team headed by party leader Peter Robinson had sought assurances that they would not see or share a room with Sinn Fein chief negotiato Martim McGuiness's delegation.

An official said the South Africans, including ANC chief negotiator Cyril Ramaphosa -- now one of the country's leading black businessmen -- and former National Party chief negotiator Roelf Meyer would brief the nine Irish parties in parallel sessions.
"There are two bars and two dining rooms and the South Africans will do every briefing twice so those who don't want to will not even have to see each other in the distance," he said.
The meeting will take place at a high-security complex used under apartheid for the development of a South African missile engine and since then mainly for conferences and sensitive negotiations.
The centre is in the De Hoop nature reserve and less than 10 km (six miles) from the small beach resort of Arniston.

The Irish participants represent the Alliance Party, the Social Democratic Labour Party, the Democratic Unionist Party, the Ulster Democratic Party, the Labour Party, the Ulster Unionist Party, the Progressive Unionist Party, the Women's Coalition and Sinn Fein.
